" src="https://img.etimg.com/thumb/msid-136093084,width-210,height-158,imgsize-53100,resizemode-75/rupee-retreats-goldman-calls-it-a-port-of-stability-in-ai-stormbr.jpg"> Agencies The Indian rupee retreated after touching a seven-month high on Monday, pausing a five-day rally driven by robust portfolio inflows amid a rotation away from crowded AI trades, with Goldman Sachs describing the unit as a "port of stability in the AI storm." The rupee rose to a peak of 92.44 in early trades, its strongest level since April, before reversing course; it was last quoted at 92.8825, compared with its previous close of 92.67. It is on course for a monthly gain of over 2% - its best since March 2025 - shored up by a foreign investor rush into local stocks that has poured $13 billion into Indian equities over November already. On Monday, a burst of corporate dollar buying weighed on the rupee after it rose in early trading, with traders pointing to such demand also coming from two large conglomerates. The rupee's early gains also pushed it into overbought territory, per a key momentum indicator. Live Events "While we remain sceptical that spot appreciation at this pace can extend given the need to rebuild external reserve buffers, there seems to be a greater commitment to allowing more two-way volatility in the currency," analysts at Goldman Sachs said in a note. India's foreign exchange reserves declined to a three-month low of about $705 billion as of November 13, according to data released on Friday. "In this type of global markets backdrop, the rupee should continue to be a port of stability in the AI storm," the note added. In addition to gaining against the dollar, the rupee has also strengthened about 4% against the British pound and the euro alongside a 3% gain against the Japanese yen over November so far. " src="https://img.etimg.com/thumb/msid-136092329,width-210,height-158,imgsize-202590,resizemode-75/the-great-indian-stock-market-comeback-can-the-rally-sustain-and-what-should-investors-dobr.jpg"> ET CONTRIBUTORS The stock market possesses an uncanny ability to surprise—and surprise it did, surging 9.7 percent in just eight trading sessions through November 12. For months, Indian equities had languished among the world’s worst-performing markets. Since February, FIIs had relentlessly pulled capital out of India in pursuit of greener pastures in the global artificial intelligence (AI) boom. Simultaneously, elevated crude oil prices strained India’s trade and current account deficits. The rupee slid to become one of emerging Asia’s weakest currencies, touching a low of ₹96.96 against the US dollar in May. All stars seemed aligned against Dalal Street . Then, at the turn of November, a rare convergence of external and domestic triggers flipped the script. The Republican rout in the US mid-term elections, with Democrats, who want strict regulation of AI, securing majorities in both the House and the Senate, sparked a sell-off in US AI stocks. The correction swiftly spilled over into other major tech hubs, including South Korea, Taiwan, and Japan. As global capital rotated out of crowded technology trades in search of credible "non-AI" alternatives, India stood out. FIIs—who had offloaded Indian equities worth $19 billion in 2025 and another $31 billion in 2026 through October—abruptly reversed course. In just eight trading days through November 12, foreign funds turned aggressive buyers, pumping ₹73,565 crore into domestic equities. Fundamental Tailwinds Beyond global liquidity rotation, improving domestic fundamentals suggest the rally has legs. Brent crude has cooled below $95 per barrel, easing pressure on India’s external balances. Live Events Consequently, the rupee has appreciated to around ₹94 against the dollar, further burnishing the appeal of Indian assets for foreign investors. More importantly, the rally is anchored by a tangible turnaround in corporate earnings. The recovery that took root in Q1 FY27 gathered momentum in Q2, putting India Inc on track for a potential 15 percent earnings growth in FY27. Meanwhile, the broader economy continues to display remarkable resilience, with GDP projected to expand at 7.3 percent in FY27—the fastest pace among major global economies. The Indian currency depreciated sharply till October, declining 8% against the US dollar at the lowest point of the year as foreign investors withdrew from equity markets in Asia's third-largest economy due to high valuations and lack of AI investments. Higher oil prices added to the pressure, prompting tough measures from the central bank, including a reserve requirement against large hedging transactions. Markets turned in November, with global investors pumping a monthly record $12 billion into Indian equities. "I believe 91.50 could be a possibility," said Arup Rakshit, group head for treasury at HDFC Bank in Mumbai in an interview late on Friday, adding that he sees the currency trading in a range of 91.50 to 93.50 in the near term. Live Events On Friday, the rupee closed at 92.67 to the dollar. The rupee has gained nearly 2.5% in November, turning sentiment in the offshore non-deliverable forwards market and prompting exporters to sell dollars, Rakshit said. Additional dollar demand brought on by the Reserve Bank of India 's decision to impose a 20% foreign exchange risk reserve on large hedging transactions has also eased, he added. "When the Reserve Bank of India introduced a foreign exchange risk reserve there was some additional dollar demand that came in from importers as absolute hedged import rates were lower, since the INR had immediately appreciated," Rakshit said. "That demand is now reducing as the import cycle is typically 90 days and nearly half of that is over," he said, adding that importers are hedging less as the rupee strengthens and oil prices fall. Agencies Four to five privately placed Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) are expected to tap the public markets by March 2027 to raise a combined Rs 17,000 crore, as infrastructure developers increasingly turn to this route to mobilise long-term capital and monetise operational assets, investment bankers said. InvITs have already mobilised around Rs 88,000 crore through equity issuances during FY23-FY25, indicating growing investor appetite for infrastructure-backed investment opportunities , according to the Bharat InvITs Association . Among the proposed public offerings, Brookfield-backed Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust has filed for a potential Rs 6,000-crore IPO as it seeks to convert from a privately placed to a publicly offered InvIT. Investcorp-backed NDR InvIT Trust is also planning to transition into a public InvIT through an issue of up to Rs 750 crore, while KKR and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan (OTPP)-sponsored Vertis Infrastructure Trust is also exploring an IPO. In March, NHAI-sponsored Raajmarg Infra Investment Trust raised Rs 6,000 crore through its IPO. Live Events The growing pipeline of public offerings comes amid an expansion in India's InvIT market, estimated at around Rs 7.5 lakh crore, as infrastructure companies increasingly look at the trust structure to unlock capital from operational assets and fund future expansion . The market is also attracting a wider pool of investors. InvITs had around 6.5 lakh unitholders as of the first quarter of FY27, and over the past 10 years, InvITs have collectively distributed nearly Rs 1 lakh crore to their investors, as per the Bharat InvITs Association. Under SEBI regulations, InvITs are required to distribute at least 90 per cent of their net distributable cash flows to unitholders, making them an attractive investment avenue for investors seeking regular income. The investor base is also gradually broadening, with a growing number of women participating as unitholders, according to brokers and wealth advisers. The sector has received a further boost from the Securities and Exchange Board of India's (SEBI) introduction of a framework for depository receipts, allowing foreign investors to gain exposure to Indian REITs and InvITs through select overseas exchanges. ET Online Reliance Brands has reported a 3.77 per cent increase in revenue to Rs 3,390.89 crore for FY26 and has narrowed its loss to Rs 137.04 crore, according to an RoC filing. Reliance Brands Ltd (RBL), a subsidiary of the country's leading retailer Reliance Retail Ventures Ltd (RRVL), operates business of global fashion and lifestyle brands in India market through strategic partnerships, brand ownership and retail operations . RBL reported revenue from operations of Rs 3,267.66 crore and a profit of Rs 237.12 crore in FY25, according to financial data accessed through the business intelligence platform Tofler. It manages a diverse and expanding portfolio of international and domestic brands across luxury, bridge-to-luxury, premium, and high-street fashion, as well as F&B, eyewear, home & lifestyle, and toys. "Operating within the discretionary consumption space, the company caters to an affluent customer base in India, estimated at 12-15 million consumers, and has established itself as the partner of choice for leading global brands," said RBL. Live Events As of March 31, 2026, the company operated 1,085 Points of Sale across India, including proprietary multi-brand concepts such as The Whitecrow, The Books & Cafe, and Tank, alongside a portfolio of over 90 partner brands. In FY26, RBL further strengthened its Fashion & Lifestyle portfolio by adding three globally recognised brands. It entered into master franchise partnerships with contemporary womenswear brands Stella McCartney and MAX&Co, as well as British luxury footwear and accessories brand Kurt Geiger, thereby enhancing its presence across premium fashion segments. The company also expanded into the high-growth athleisure and activewear category through a master franchise partnership with Fabletics, launching a new portfolio vertical and reinforcing its commitment to capturing evolving consumer lifestyle trends. "During the year under review, your company achieved a net turnover of Rs 3,390.89 crore as compared to Rs 3,267.66 crore during last year. The company registered a loss of Rs 137.13 crore as compared to Rs 233.79 crore during last year," it said. RBL has six subsidiaries, 11 joint ventures and four associate companies. In addition to building international brand partnerships , the company has invested in leading Indian designer labels and made key global acquisitions, including Hamleys, the world's oldest toy retailer, now operating across 13 countries.
